# Spec: Home page transform (Streamline) — v1

## Goal
Replace the stock Jellyfin home page with the approved concept
`docs/design/home-concept-gpt.html`: quiet top bar, cinematic billboard that doubles as a
one-tap resume surface, then edge-to-edge rails — Continue Watching (landscape, progress),
Shows (posters), Movies (posters). Same injected-JS approach and lifecycle discipline as the
detail transform in js/theme.js.

## Route + mount
- Hijack the HOME route only (verify exact 10.11 hash from the bundle — likely `#/home.html`;
  also handle the empty-hash boot default that lands on home). All other routes untouched.
- Mount `#streamline-home` as an overlay of the visible home page element (verify container id
  in the live DOM — likely `#indexPage:not(.hide)`), same absolute-overlay + `position:relative`
  parent trick as the detail view.
- Add `body.streamline-home-active` while mounted, hiding `.skinHeader` and the native home
  content (scope to the visible home page; verify selectors live and pin them in
  docs/jellyfin-10.11-notes.md). Restore on teardown/dispose — same rules as
  `streamline-series-active`.
- Reuse: `el()`, `imageUrl()`, `applyAccent` (accent applies here too), gen-counter guards,
  silent degrade, id-guarded container, teardown on hashchange, `dispose()` cleanup.

## Top bar
- Wordmark "Streamline" (text + the small CSS mark from the concept).
- Search icon button (inline SVG, ≥44px) → navigate to the native search route (verify hash,
  likely `#/search.html`).
- Avatar button (first letter of `ApiClient.getCurrentUser()` name, cached; concept's gradient
  disc) → navigate to the native user-preferences menu route (verify, likely
  `#/mypreferencesmenu.html`).

## Data + sections (all via ApiClient; skip a section silently if its fetch fails or is empty)
1. **Continue Watching** = resumable items then next-up:
   - Resume: `GET /Users/{uid}/Items/Resume?Recursive=true&Limit=12&MediaTypes=Video&Fields=Overview`
     (use the ApiClient helper if present — verify name in bundle, e.g. `getResumableItems`).
   - Next up: `getNextUpEpisodes({ UserId, Limit: 12, Fields: 'Overview' })`.
   - Merge: resume items first, then next-up episodes whose SeriesId is not already represented.
   - Landscape cards: art (episode Primary → Backdrop fallback), white play-chip bottom-left,
     progress bar when PlaybackPositionTicks > 0, title = SeriesName (episodes) / Name (movies),
     sub = `S1:E3 · 12 min left` (episodes) or `N min left` / `Xh Ym` (movies).
   - Tap on the card art/play-chip → play directly via the existing `playItem()` delegation.
     Tap on the title/sub area → navigate to the item's (series'/movie's) detail page. If that
     split is awkward to implement accessibly, the whole card navigates to detail and ONLY the
     play-chip plays — chip must then be its own ≥44px button.
2. **Billboard hero** = first Continue Watching entry; fallback: first Series with a backdrop;
   if none, omit the hero. Real backdrop image as background (Backdrop maxWidth 1280) under the
   concept's gradient scrims. Kicker "Continue watching" (or "Featured" for the fallback),
   big title, meta line, 2-line summary clamp, actions: primary `▶ Resume`/`▶ Play` (plays via
   `playItem`) + secondary `ⓘ Details` (navigates to detail).
3. **Shows**: `Items?IncludeItemTypes=Series&Recursive=true&SortBy=SortName&Fields=ChildCount`
   → poster cards (Primary image), sub `N season(s)`. Tap → detail.
4. **Movies**: same with `IncludeItemTypes=Movie` → sub `YYYY · Xh Ym`. Tap → detail.
- No "See all" links in v1 (small library; rails hold everything).

## CSS
- New section in css/view.css under `#streamline-home` using the concept's tokens (reuse
  existing `--sl-*` vars; hero/rail/card styles adapted from the concept file, including the
  560px phone breakpoint, scroll-snap rails, hidden scrollbars, active-press scale, and
  reduced-motion guards). No borders on cards. All tap targets ≥44px.

## Out of scope (v1)
Library "See all" views, search/profile redesign (native pages), genre rows, per-user row
customization.

## Verification (computer-use, iPad Pro 11" + phone width 412px)
- Home renders our view (no native header/sections visible); billboard shows a real backdrop
  and Resume works via delegation spy (no playback started).
- Rails scroll horizontally; Continue Watching shows progress + correct sublabels; Shows has
  3 posters with season counts; Movies has 7 with year·runtime.
- Tap a poster → Streamline detail page mounts; back → home re-mounts cleanly (no dupes ×3).
- Search + avatar buttons land on the native pages with header restored.
- Accent preset applies to home (play chips/progress/primary button).
- No console errors referencing streamline assets.
# Streamline — a Jellyfin theme

Modern streaming-style UI for our self-hosted **Jellyfin** (v10.11) media server, delivered as
**injected JavaScript + CSS**. It transforms the stock TV-show detail page into a
Netflix/Disney+-style combined show → seasons → episodes view. Viewed in the Jellyfin mobile
app (a webview) on tablets/phones.

**Status: DEPLOYED** (2026-07-19). Served automatically by the live server via a custom
web-dir (`scripts/webdir/`, see `docs/delivery.md`) — no manual injection. Owner approved the
look. Per-user accent color is choosable in the user's Display settings. Verified on an iPad
Pro 11" viewport; real-phone check by the owner is the remaining step — see
[Where we are](#where-we-are).

## Why injected JS+CSS (not a plugin, not just CSS)
- **Jellyfin plugins** are server-side .NET — they cannot touch the web UI. Wrong tool.
- **Custom CSS alone** (branding box) can only style/hide/clamp (~60%). It cannot restructure
  the DOM (single hero, one Play pill, combined view, working "show more"). So we need JS.
- **Injected JS** runs in the authenticated page, can call the full REST API via
  `window.ApiClient`, and can render our own view. This is the approach.

## The design
Approved concept: **`docs/design/gpt-concept-APPROVED.html`** (open in a browser). The six
fixes it bakes in (all implemented):
1. One primary **Play** pill + heart + overflow (no shuffle / mark-played).
2. Single cinematic hero, **no** redundant poster card.
3. Tight header → content above the fold.
4. Episode descriptions **clamped to 2 lines**.
5. **"Show more" actually toggles** (and hides itself when text doesn't overflow).
6. **No per-episode heart.**

Also in `docs/design/`: `grok-concept.html` (the cleaner Netflix-clone alt, not chosen),
`sewerstream-goham-*.html` (fun over-the-top TMNT skins — NOT for implementation), `brief.md`.

## Architecture
Targeted **route hijack** of the **series** detail route only (`#/details?id=<seriesId>`):
- `js/theme.js` watches the SPA hash, and when a *Series* detail route is shown, renders our
  own `#streamline-detail` view (styled by `css/view.css`) into the native `#itemDetailPage`,
  covering it. Data comes from `window.ApiClient` (getItem / getSeasons / getEpisodes /
  getNextUpEpisodes / getImageUrl).
- **Playback delegates to Jellyfin's native controls** (its `playbackManager` is a module
  export, not a global, so we can't call it directly): the Play pill clicks the native
  `.btnPlay`; an episode navigates to its detail hash and clicks that page's native play.
- Everything else (home, library grids, search, the video player, season/episode detail
  pages) stays **stock**. Lifecycle is route-keyed with a versioned global sentinel
  (`window.__streamlineTheme`) so re-injection disposes the prior instance.

See `specs/show-detail-transform.md` for the full spec and `docs/jellyfin-10.11-notes.md` for
the hard-won DOM/API facts (verified against live 10.11 markup).

## Repo layout
```
css/theme.css     branding-box CSS (Ultrachromic import + hide/clamp) — styles STOCK Jellyfin
css/view.css      styles ONLY the injected #streamline-detail custom view
js/theme.js       the route-hijack + custom render (v2)
specs/            implementation specs (detail transform, webdir delivery, accent preference)
docs/design/      approved concept + alternates + brief
docs/reviews/     gpt spec reviews + grok implementation reviews
docs/delivery.md  how production delivery works + upgrade/caching/TCC notes
docs/verification-recipe.md   how to verify against the live server (login inject, screenshot)
docs/jellyfin-10.11-notes.md  DOM selectors, ApiClient facts, gotchas
scripts/webdir/   build-webdir.sh (webdir copy + tag injection), launcher, LaunchAgent template
scripts/ripping/  DVD-rip renaming helpers (rename_show.sh, courage_titles.txt)
scripts/ripper/   two-drive automated TMNT ripping pipeline (see specs/ripper-pipeline.md)
```

## Where we are
DONE (as of 2026-07-19):
1. **Production delivery LIVE** — custom web-dir at
   `~/Library/Application Support/jellyfin/streamline-web/`, built by
   `scripts/webdir/build-webdir.sh` (hashed asset names beat the service-worker cache; tags
   injected with marker comments; idempotent). Server runs with `--webdir` pointing at it.
   Re-run the build script after editing theme files or upgrading Jellyfin (`docs/delivery.md`).
2. **Per-user accent color** — 6 presets, picker injected into the user's Display settings
   (`#/mypreferencesdisplay`), stored server-side in DisplayPreferences CustomPrefs
   (`streamlineAccent`), localStorage mirror for instant paint. Spec-reviewed by gpt (11
   must-fixes applied), implementation-reviewed by grok (P0 + fixes applied, see docs/reviews/).
3. **Verified on iPad Pro 11" viewport** (gpt computer-use): auto-delivery, layout, play
   delegation, accent persistence incl. native-Save reconciliation, route cleanup.

NOT DONE:
1. **Owner phone check** in the real mobile app webview (emulated iPad ≠ real device).
2. Only the **Series** page is transformed; season/episode pages stay native (intentional).
3. Optional polish from grok's original review: AbortController for in-flight fetches,
   per-season episode caching.

## How we work on this (multi-agent pipeline)
Claude specs → **gpt** (codex, Sol tier) reviews the spec → Claude implements → **grok**
(cursor-agent) reviews the implementation → Claude verifies any factual dispute against the
live DOM (authoritative) → screenshot to owner. Both review docs are in `docs/reviews/`.
/* Jellyfin Streamline — theme.js  (v2)
 * Route-scoped hijack of Series and Movie detail views. Renders custom Netflix/Disney+-style
 * show->seasons->episodes and movie views from the Jellyfin REST API (via window.ApiClient).
 * Playback delegates to Jellyfin's native controls (playbackManager is a module export, not global):
 *   - series Play  -> click the native .btnPlay (data-action="resume") on the series page
 *   - an episode   -> navigate to its detail hash, then click that page's native play control
 * Verified against live Jellyfin 10.11 markup: primary=.btnPlay[data-action=resume],
 *   from-start=.btnReplay[data-action=play] (hidden), overflow=.btnMoreCommands.
 * Reinjection-safe via a versioned global sentinel with dispose().
 */
(function () {
  'use strict';
  var VERSION = 3;
  if (window.__streamlineTheme && typeof window.__streamlineTheme.dispose === 'function') {
    try { window.__streamlineTheme.dispose(); } catch (e) {}
  }

  var CONTAINER_ID = 'streamline-detail';
  var ACTIVE_CLASS = 'streamline-series-active';
  var gen = 0;
  var mounted = null;          // { el, page, pagePrevPosition }
  var hashHandler = null;
  var accentObserver = null;
  var accentPicker = null;     // { section, form, submitHandler, targetUserId, confirmed, selected }
  var accentCache = {};
  var accentQueue = Promise.resolve();
  var accentSelectionGen = 0;
  var knownCurrentUserId = null;
  var timeoutIds = [];
  var initInterval = null;
  var accentMountTimer = null;
  var ACCENT_PREF = 'streamlineAccent';
  var ACCENTS = {
    violet: { name: 'Violet', accent: '#7c5cff', ink: '#0a0713' },
    sky: { name: 'Sky', accent: '#38bdf8', ink: '#041018' },
    mint: { name: 'Mint', accent: '#34d399', ink: '#04150c' },
    amber: { name: 'Amber', accent: '#fbbf24', ink: '#1a1002' },
    coral: { name: 'Coral', accent: '#fb7185', ink: '#1c040a' },
    mono: { name: 'Mono', accent: '#e2e8f0', ink: '#0b0b0d' }
  };
  var ACCENT_IDS = ['violet', 'sky', 'mint', 'amber', 'coral', 'mono'];

  // ---------- helpers ----------
  function api() { return window.ApiClient; }
  function userId() { return api() && api().getCurrentUserId(); }
  function validAccent(id) { return typeof id === 'string' && !!ACCENTS[id]; }
  function scheduleTimeout(callback, delay) {
    var id = setTimeout(function () {
      var index = timeoutIds.indexOf(id);
      if (index !== -1) timeoutIds.splice(index, 1);
      callback();
    }, delay);
    timeoutIds.push(id);
    return id;
  }
  function cancelTimeout(id) {
    if (id === null || typeof id === 'undefined') return;
    clearTimeout(id);
    var index = timeoutIds.indexOf(id);
    if (index !== -1) timeoutIds.splice(index, 1);
  }
  function clearScheduledWork() {

    accentMountTimer = null;
    if (initInterval !== null) { clearInterval(initInterval); initInterval = null; }
  }
  function serverId() {
    try { return api() && api().serverId(); } catch (e) { return null; }
  }
  function accentKey(uid) {
    var sid = serverId();
    return sid && uid ? sid + '.' + uid : null;
  }
  function accentStorageKey(uid) {
    var key = accentKey(uid);
    return key ? 'streamline.accent.' + key : null;
  }
  function checkAuth() {
    var current = userId() || null;
    if (knownCurrentUserId !== current) {

      knownCurrentUserId = current;

    }
    return current;
  }
  function cachedAccent(uid) {
    if (!uid || !checkAuth()) return null;
    var key = accentKey(uid);
    if (!key) return null;
    if (!accentCache[key]) {

  }

    var entry = accentCache[key] || { loaded: false, value: null, inflight: null };
    entry.loaded = true; entry.value = value;

    try {
      if (value) localStorage.setItem(storageKey, value);
      else localStorage.removeItem(storageKey);
    } catch (e) {}
  }
  function applyAccent(root, presetId) {

    (children || []).forEach(function (c) { if (c) n.appendChild(c); });
    return n;
  }
  function imageUrl(item, type, maxWidth) {
    var tags = item.ImageTags || {};
    var tag = type === 'Backdrop' ? (item.BackdropImageTags || [])[0] : tags[type];
    if (!tag) return null;

    if (btn) { btn.click(); if (cb) cb(true); return; }

        el('div', { className: 'sl-ep-title', text: (ep.IndexNumber ? ep.IndexNumber + '. ' : '') + (ep.Name || '') }),
        el('div', { className: 'sl-ep-run', text: ep.RunTimeTicks ? ticksToMin(ep.RunTimeTicks) + 'm' : '' }),
        ep.Overview ? el('div', { className: 'sl-ep-desc', text: ep.Overview }) : null
      ])
    ]);
    row.addEventListener('click', function () { playItem(ep.Id); });
    return row;
  }
  function seasonCard(season, onSelect) {
    var card = el('button', { className: 'sl-season', type: 'button', 'aria-selected': 'false' }, [
      el('div', { className: 'sl-s-num', text: season.Name || ('Season ' + (season.IndexNumber || '')) }),
      el('div', { className: 'sl-s-count', text: (season.ChildCount || 0) + ' episodes' })
    ]);
    card.addEventListener('click', function () { onSelect(season, card); });
    return card;
  }
  function specialFeatures(uid, itemId) {
    if (typeof api().getSpecialFeatures === 'function') return api().getSpecialFeatures(uid, itemId);
    return api().ajax({
      type: 'GET',
      url: api().getUrl('Users/' + uid + '/Items/' + itemId + '/SpecialFeatures'),
      dataType: 'json'
    });
  }
  function extraRow(item) {
    var row = el('button', { className: 'sl-extra', type: 'button' }, [
      thumb(item),
/* Jellyfin Streamline — view.css
 * Styles ONLY the injected #streamline-detail custom detail view so it can't fight the stock UI.
 * Accent is a variable — owner did not commit to lime; default is a friendly violet-blue. */

/* Jellyfin 10.11's iPad layout paints these above the page-local overlay. Keep the native
 * controls in the DOM (without Jellyfin's .hide class) for playback and overflow delegation. */
body.streamline-series-active .skinHeader,
body.streamline-series-active #itemDetailPage:not(.hide) > .detailPageWrapperContainer > .detailPagePrimaryContainer > .detailRibbon {
  display: none !important;
}

#streamline-detail {
  --sl-accent: #7c5cff;
  --sl-accent-ink: #0a0713;
  --sl-bg: #0b0b0d;
  --sl-fg: #f4f4f6;
  --sl-dim: #a8a8b3;
  --sl-card: #16161a;
  --sl-radius: 16px;
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  z-index: 1;
  background: var(--sl-bg);
  color: var(--sl-fg);
  font: 15px/1.4 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;
  overflow-y: auto;
  -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch;
  padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 24px);
}

/* ---- hero (single cinematic backdrop, title overlaid, no poster card) ---- */
#streamline-detail .sl-hero {
  position: relative; width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 16 / 10;
  background-size: cover; background-position: center; background-color: #111;
}
#streamline-detail .sl-hero::after {
  content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 0;
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(11,11,13,0) 35%, rgba(11,11,13,0.65) 72%, var(--sl-bg) 100%);
}
#streamline-detail .sl-hero-title {
  position: absolute; left: 16px; right: 16px; bottom: 12px; z-index: 1; margin: 0;
  font-size: 30px; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: -0.5px; text-shadow: 0 2px 18px rgba(0,0,0,0.6);
}
#streamline-detail .sl-back {
  position: absolute; top: calc(10px + env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)); left: 12px; z-index: 2;
  width: 38px; height: 38px; border-radius: 50%; border: none;
  background: rgba(0,0,0,0.45); color: #fff; font-size: 24px; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer;
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
}
/* row elements rendered as <button> need appearance reset */
#streamline-detail .sl-continue, #streamline-detail .sl-ep, #streamline-detail .sl-season, #streamline-detail .sl-extra {
  appearance: none; -webkit-appearance: none; background: none; border: none; font: inherit; color: inherit; text-align: left; width: 100%;
}
#streamline-detail .sl-play[disabled] { opacity: 0.55; }
#streamline-detail button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--sl-accent); outline-offset: 2px; }

/* ---- metadata line (one tight row) ---- */
#streamline-detail .sl-meta { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; flex-wrap: wrap; padding: 10px 16px 0; color: var(--sl-dim); font-size: 13px; }
#streamline-detail .sl-badge { border: 1px solid #3a3a42; border-radius: 4px; padding: 1px 6px; font-size: 12px; color: var(--sl-fg); }

/* ---- actions: one primary Play pill + heart + overflow ---- */
#streamline-detail .sl-actions { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 14px 16px 4px; }
#streamline-detail .sl-play { flex: 1; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; background: var(--sl-accent); color: var(--sl-accent-ink); border: none; border-radius: 999px; padding: 14px 18px; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; min-height: 48px; }
#streamline-detail .sl-play:active { filter: brightness(0.92); }
#streamline-detail .sl-icon-btn { width: 48px; height: 48px; flex: 0 0 48px; border-radius: 999px; background: #1e1e24; border: none; color: var(--sl-fg); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-size: 20px; cursor: pointer; }
#streamline-detail .sl-icon-btn[aria-pressed="true"] { color: #ff5b7f; }

/* ---- synopsis with working clamp/expand ---- */
#streamline-detail .sl-synopsis { padding: 10px 16px 0; }
#streamline-detail .sl-synopsis p { margin: 0; color: #d7d7de; display: -webkit-box; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden; }
#streamline-detail .sl-synopsis[data-expanded="false"] p { -webkit-line-clamp: 3; }
#streamline-detail .sl-synopsis[data-expanded="true"] p { -webkit-line-clamp: unset; }
#streamline-detail .sl-more { background: none; border: none; color: var(--sl-accent); font-weight: 600; padding: 6px 0; cursor: pointer; font-size: 14px; }

/* ---- section headers ---- */
#streamline-detail .sl-section { padding: 18px 16px 0; }
#streamline-detail .sl-section > h2 { margin: 0 0 10px; font-size: 18px; font-weight: 700; }

/* ---- continue watching card ---- */
#streamline-detail .sl-continue { display: flex; gap: 12px; background: var(--sl-card); border-radius: var(--sl-radius); padding: 10px; align-items: center; }
#streamline-detail .sl-thumb { position: relative; border-radius: 10px; overflow: hidden; background: #222; }
#streamline-detail .sl-continue .sl-thumb { width: 132px; flex: 0 0 132px; aspect-ratio: 16/9; }
#streamline-detail .sl-thumb img { width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: cover; display: block; }
#streamline-detail .sl-progress { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 4px; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.25); }
#streamline-detail .sl-progress > i { display: block; height: 100%; background: var(--sl-accent); }
#streamline-detail .sl-movie-progress { position: absolute; z-index: 2; left: 16px; right: 16px; bottom: 0; height: 3px; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.25); }
#streamline-detail .sl-movie-progress > i { display: block; height: 100%; background: var(--sl-accent); }
#streamline-detail .sl-c-title { font-weight: 700; font-size: 15px; }
#streamline-detail .sl-c-sub { color: var(--sl-dim); font-size: 13px; margin-top: 2px; }

/* ---- seasons rail ---- */
#streamline-detail .sl-seasons { display: flex; gap: 10px; overflow-x: auto; padding-bottom: 4px; scrollbar-width: none; }
#streamline-detail .sl-seasons::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }
#streamline-detail .sl-season { flex: 0 0 128px; background: var(--sl-card); border: 2px solid transparent; border-radius: 12px; padding: 10px; cursor: pointer; text-align: left; color: inherit; }
#streamline-detail .sl-season[aria-selected="true"] { border-color: var(--sl-accent); }
#streamline-detail .sl-s-num { font-weight: 700; }
#streamline-detail .sl-s-count { color: var(--sl-dim); font-size: 12px; margin-top: 2px; }

/* ---- episode list (2-line clamp, no per-episode heart) ---- */
#streamline-detail .sl-episodes { margin-top: 4px; }
#streamline-detail .sl-ep { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 132px 1fr auto; gap: 12px; align-items: start; padding: 12px 0; cursor: pointer; }
#streamline-detail .sl-ep .sl-thumb { width: 132px; aspect-ratio: 16/9; }
#streamline-detail .sl-watched { position: absolute; top: 6px; right: 6px; width: 20px; height: 20px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--sl-accent); color: var(--sl-accent-ink); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-size: 13px; }
#streamline-detail .sl-ep-title { font-weight: 700; font-size: 15px; }
#streamline-detail .sl-ep-run { color: var(--sl-dim); font-size: 12px; margin: 2px 0 4px; }
#streamline-detail .sl-ep-desc { color: #c3c3cc; font-size: 13px; display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 2; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden; }
#streamline-detail .sl-ep-more { align-self: center; background: none; border: none; color: var(--sl-dim); font-size: 20px; cursor: pointer; padding: 0 4px; }

/* ---- movie extras ---- */
#streamline-detail .sl-extras { padding-bottom: 20px; }
#streamline-detail .sl-extra { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 8px 0; cursor: pointer; }
#streamline-detail .sl-extra .sl-thumb { width: 132px; flex: 0 0 132px; aspect-ratio: 16/9; }
#streamline-detail .sl-extra-copy { min-width: 0; }
#streamline-detail .sl-extra-title { font-weight: 700; font-size: 15px; }
#streamline-detail .sl-extra-run { color: var(--sl-dim); font-size: 12px; margin-top: 2px; }

/* loading / error */
#streamline-detail .sl-status { padding: 40px 16px; text-align: center; color: var(--sl-dim); }

/* ---- Display settings accent picker ---- */
.sl-accent-picker { margin-top: 2em; }
.sl-accent-picker .sl-accent-options { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 14px; align-items: center; }
.sl-accent-picker .sl-accent-swatch {
  appearance: none; -webkit-appearance: none; position: relative; width: 44px; height: 44px;
  min-width: 44px; min-height: 44px; padding: 0; border: 3px solid transparent; border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--sl-swatch); color: var(--sl-swatch-ink); cursor: pointer;
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
}
.sl-accent-picker .sl-accent-swatch[aria-checked="true"] {
  border-color: #fff; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--sl-swatch), 0 0 0 6px #fff;
}
.sl-accent-picker .sl-accent-check { font-size: 22px; font-weight: 900; line-height: 1; opacity: 0; }
.sl-accent-picker .sl-accent-swatch[aria-checked="true"] .sl-accent-check { opacity: 1; }
.sl-accent-picker .sl-accent-swatch:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #fff; outline-offset: 7px; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { #streamline-detail * { animation: none !important; transition: none !important; } }
# Jellyfin 10.11 web-client facts (verified)

Hard-won facts about the stock web client, verified against the live 10.11 DOM and/or the
jellyfin-web v10.11.8 source (gpt cloned + grepped it during spec review). These are what the
transform depends on — re-verify if Jellyfin is upgraded.

## Globals / modules
- `window.ApiClient` **IS** exposed (set in `ServerConnections.js`: `window.ApiClient = apiClient`).
  Use its helpers — do NOT hand-build URLs or put tokens in image URLs:
  - `ApiClient.getCurrentUserId()`
  - `ApiClient.getItem(userId, itemId)`
  - `ApiClient.getSeasons(seriesId, { userId, Fields:'ChildCount' })`  ← Fields MUST be `ChildCount` for episode counts; `ItemCounts` does NOT populate `ChildCount`.
  - `ApiClient.getEpisodes(seriesId, { seasonId, userId, Fields:'Overview' })`
  - `ApiClient.getNextUpEpisodes({ SeriesId, UserId, Fields:'Overview', Limit:1 })`
  - `ApiClient.getImageUrl(itemId, { type:'Primary'|'Backdrop', tag, maxWidth })`
  - `ApiClient.updateFavoriteStatus(userId, itemId, isFavorite)` → Promise
- `playbackManager` is a **module export** (`export const playbackManager = new PlaybackManager()`
  in `components/playback/playbackmanager.js`), NOT a global. Injected code cannot import it.
  → **Delegate playback to native controls** instead.

## Item detail page — native markup (in `.mainDetailButtons`, page `#itemDetailPage`)
Verified by dumping the live buttons:
| Button | class | data-action | notes |
|--------|-------|-------------|-------|
| Play / Resume (primary) | `.btnPlay` | `resume` | VISIBLE. Click this for "Play" (native resume/play). |
| Play from start | `.btnReplay` | `play` | HIDDEN unless resume available. |
| Shuffle | `.btnShuffle` | — | (a fix removes it from our UI) |
| Mark played (check) | `.btnPlaystate` (`emby-playstatebutton`) | — | (removed from our UI) |
| Favorite (heart) | `.btnUserRating` (`emby-ratingbutton`) | — | we use the API instead |
| Overflow (…) | `.btnMoreCommands` | — | wire our ⋯ to click this for a real menu |
| Download / Trailer / InstantMix / Split / timers | `.btnDownload` etc. | — | usually `.hide` |
- `.btnResume` does **NOT** exist (an early wrong guess). Resume is `.btnPlay[data-action=resume]`.
- The visible detail page is `#itemDetailPage:not(.hide)` with `offsetParent !== null`. A
  `.itemDetailPage` can exist hidden after SPA transitions — always gate on visibility.
- Native bind race: `.btnPlay` may be present but not yet wired right after route change;
  our code retries the click briefly and disables the Play pill until `.btnPlay:not(.hide)` exists.

### iPad-UA pinned detail header
- Verified at 834×1194, DPR 2, touch, iPad Safari UA against the live 10.11 UI:
  - `.skinHeader` is a sibling/outside ancestor of `#itemDetailPage`, with `position: fixed` and
    `z-index: 999`; it forms the top app bar and therefore cannot be covered by an absolute
    overlay inside the detail page.
  - `#itemDetailPage:not(.hide) > .detailPageWrapperContainer > .detailPagePrimaryContainer >
    .detailRibbon` has `position: relative` and `z-index: 2`. It contains `.infoWrapper`
    (poster thumbnail, centered title/metadata) and `.mainDetailButtons` (play, shuffle,
    play-state, favorite, and overflow). It paints above `#streamline-detail` (`z-index: 1`).
- While a Streamline Series view is mounted, `body.streamline-series-active` hides the native
  `.skinHeader` and visible page `.detailRibbon` with Streamline-owned CSS. Do not add Jellyfin's
  `.hide` class: `.btnPlay:not(.hide)` readiness/delegation and `.btnMoreCommands:not(.hide)`
  overflow delegation must continue to find and click the native controls.

## Custom-view DOM classes (stock detail page, for CSS-only hiding if ever needed)
- Synopsis paragraph: `.overview` (also `.detail-clamp-text`) — NOT `.overview-text`.
- Metadata rows: `.genresGroup`, `.studiosGroup`, `.itemTags`, `.itemExternalLinks`.
- Cast: `#castCollapsible`.

## Display preferences page and Save behavior
- Verified by read-only grep of the installed macOS bundle at
  `/Applications/Jellyfin.app/Contents/Resources/jellyfin-web` (the
  `user-display.*.chunk.js` and `user-display-index-tsx.*.chunk.js` chunks).
- The React Display page renders with `id="displayPreferencesPage"`, and its settings container
  contains a single `<form>`. Therefore `#displayPreferencesPage form` is the verified picker
  mount selector for this installed 10.11 bundle.
- The Save control is rendered inside that form with `type="submit"`. The form has an `onSubmit`
  handler that calls `preventDefault()` and then the native `submitChanges()` path. A native DOM
  `submit` listener on the form therefore observes Save activation; a separate click-only hook is
  not required for this bundle.

## Playback for a specific episode
No global playbackManager → navigate to the episode's detail hash
(`location.hash = '#/details?id=<episodeId>'`), wait for that page's
`.mainDetailButtons .btnPlay/.btnReplay`, and click it. Our route watcher only mounts on
`Type === 'Series'`, so Episode/Season detail pages stay native and this delegation works.

## Delivery / production caveats (from gpt spec review, docs/reviews/)
- Bundled `index.html` is macOS App-Management-protected (can't edit in place).
- Inline `<script>`/`<style>` may be blocked by CSP in prod — prefer external `<script src>`/`<link>`.
- The **service worker** can serve a cached old app shell — version injected asset URLs.
- The mobile webview differs from desktop Chrome (safe-area insets, autoplay gestures, back
  button, layout) — test in the real app, don't assume parity.
- `/Branding/Css` is hard-cached by the client; changes need a hard reload / app force-close.

Change the spec to match `^#/home(?:[?]|$)` and state that `""`, `"#"`, and `"#/"` must remain untouched while waiting for Jellyfin’s redirect to `#/home`; do not mount against those ambiguous states because they can also precede login/server-selection routing.

2. **Initialization waits for the wrong readiness condition.** Quote: “same lifecycle discipline as the detail transform in `js/theme.js`.” The existing transform initializes as soon as `window.ApiClient` exists, but on first authenticated boot the client can exist before `getCurrentUserId()` returns a user. A one-shot home fetch would then fail silently and never retry because the eventual sign-in does not necessarily change the hash. Require readiness for all three conditions: route is `#/home`, `ApiClient` exists, and `ApiClient.getCurrentUserId()` is non-empty. Retry with a bounded/disposable timer and also react to Jellyfin sign-in/sign-out/API-client events or an equivalent observer. Teardown immediately if the authenticated user changes.

3. **The mount selector needs visibility and identity rules.** Quote: “likely `#indexPage:not(.hide)`.” The installed React home component renders `<div id="indexPage" class="mainAnimatedPage homePage …">`; `#indexPage` is correct. Change the spec to require `#indexPage.homePage:not(.hide)` plus an actual visibility/connection check such as `isConnected && offsetParent !== null`. Jellyfin can retain SPA pages, and an ID lookup alone can target a cached/transitioning page. Store the exact page node in `mounted` and reject all asynchronous work if that node is disconnected or no longer visible.

4. **Hashchange alone is not a sufficient home lifecycle.** Quote: “teardown on hashchange.” Home is a React route whose page node and children can appear after the hash changes, be restored without a new hash, or be replaced during SPA reconciliation. Require a bounded mount retry after routing plus a page/root observer that detects `#indexPage` replacement or removal. The observer, retry timers, requestAnimationFrame callbacks, and event handlers must all be disconnected/cancelled by teardown and `dispose()`.

5. **Native home tabs are not addressed.** Quote: “Hijack the HOME route only” and “native home content … hidden.” The installed home page contains two tabs, `#homeTab` and `#favoritesTab`, and restores the selected tab through Jellyfin’s tab controller. Both share the same `#/home` hash, so a hash-only transform can cover a restored Favorites tab while Jellyfin still believes Favorites is selected. Specify one policy explicitly: v1 replaces the entire `#/home` route, hides/disables the native header tabs, and does not expose Favorites; or only mounts when native tab index 0 is selected and tears down on tab changes. The stated goal implies the first policy, but it must be explicit and verified after tab restoration.

6. **The native-content hiding selector is dangerously underspecified.** Quote: “hiding `.skinHeader` and the native home content (scope to the visible home page).” A broad descendant rule can hide `#streamline-home` along with the native content. Pin exact selectors. For this bundle, the native content roots are the direct home tab contents under `#indexPage`, including `#homeTab` and `#favoritesTab`; hide those or their native `.sections`, never arbitrary children of `#indexPage`. Add the verified selectors to `docs/jellyfin-10.11-notes.md` as requested by the spec.

7. **`getCurrentUser()` is asynchronous.** Quote: “first letter of `ApiClient.getCurrentUser()` name, cached.” In the installed API client, `getCurrentUser()` returns a Promise and rejects when no current user ID exists. Change this to: render a neutral accessible avatar initially, call `ApiClient.getCurrentUser().then(user => user.Name)`, cache by server ID plus user ID, and guard completion with the generation, mounted root, and current-user identity. Clear the cache on sign-out/user change.

8. **API facts should be made exact rather than left as guesses.** Quote: “use the ApiClient helper if present — verify name in bundle, e.g. `getResumableItems`.” The installed helper is exactly `ApiClient.getResumableItems(userId, options)` and it calls `Users/{uid}/Items/Resume`. Require that helper with:
   `getResumableItems(uid, { Recursive:true, Limit:12, MediaTypes:'Video', Fields:'Overview' })`.
   It returns the normal query-result object, so consume `result.Items || []`. Keep `getNextUpEpisodes({ UserId:uid, Limit:12, Fields:'Overview' })`. For Shows and Movies, specify `ApiClient.getItems(uid, options)` rather than an ambiguous raw `Items?…` request.

9. **Data orchestration cannot implement the stated hero fallback as independent section fetches.** Quote: “Billboard hero = first Continue Watching entry; fallback: first Series with a backdrop.” Continue Watching and Shows may resolve in either order. Require a single render orchestration using `Promise.allSettled` or equivalent: normalize each result, compute the merged Continue Watching list, then select the hero from that list or the first fetched Series with a usable `BackdropImageTags[0]`. Each rail may still degrade independently, but hero selection must wait until both relevant outcomes are known.

10. **The Continue Watching merge rule is incomplete.** Quote: “then next-up episodes whose `SeriesId` is not already represented.” Define the represented-series set using only non-empty `SeriesId` values from resumable episodes. Movies and other resumable videos must not add `undefined` to the set and accidentally suppress unrelated next-up rows. Also specify deduplication by item ID across both responses and whether multiple resumable episodes from one series are intentionally retained; otherwise the output varies with server ordering.

11. **Detail navigation needs an exact target rule.** Quote: “navigate to the item’s (series’/movie’s) detail page.” For an episode card, distinguish playback target from details target: play uses the episode `Id`; Details uses `SeriesId`; movies use their own `Id`. If `SeriesId` is absent, fall back to the item’s own detail page. Encode IDs with `encodeURIComponent` and navigate to the verified route `#/details?id=<id>`. Without this rule, implementations will commonly open episode details instead of the requested series page.

12. **Back-stack semantics must distinguish Details from playback delegation.** Quote: “Tap a poster → Streamline detail page mounts; back → home re-mounts cleanly.” Require Details navigation to push a normal history entry so one Back returns to `#/home`. Preserve the existing detail transform’s `history.back()` behavior. Separately document that `playItem()` temporarily navigates through the concrete item’s native detail page before invoking playback; this can leave an episode-detail entry in the native playback back stack. Either accept and test that behavior explicitly or define a different supported delegation strategy—do not claim one-back-to-home behavior for playback without verifying it.

13. **State restoration is unspecified.** Quote: “back → home re-mounts cleanly.” Clean remounting does not guarantee usable restoration: teardown destroys the custom root and loses vertical position and every rail’s horizontal position. Require a per-server/per-user in-memory view-state record containing root `scrollTop` and each rail’s `scrollLeft`, captured before navigating to Details and restored after the home layout mounts. Reset it on sign-out and full disposal. Also state whether a normal fresh Home navigation starts at the top.

14. **Generation checks alone do not protect every nested failure path.** Quote: “gen-counter guards, silent degrade.” Require every success and failure callback—including episode/detail navigation polling, avatar loading, accent loading, image-dependent hero selection, and section rendering—to check generation, current user ID, root identity, and `root.isConnected`. A stale `.catch()` must not clear or replace content belonging to a newer mount. Prefer `AbortController` for fetches where supported, with generation checks retained as the final guard.

15. **Playback readiness from Home is not specified.** Quote: “plays via `playItem`.” The existing `playItem()` changes the hash and polls for a visible native detail page, but it can accidentally see the outgoing cached detail page during a rapid transition. Require polling to verify that the visible page represents the requested item—through its route/current item identity—not merely that any `.btnPlay` exists. All polling timers must be cancelled on generation change/dispose, and the button should surface or recover from timeout rather than silently doing nothing.

16. **Verified native routes should replace the guesses.** Quote: “likely `#/search.html`” and “likely `#/mypreferencesmenu.html`.” The installed routes are exactly `#/search` and `#/mypreferencesmenu`. Change both links accordingly. Prefer Jellyfin’s navigation facility when safely accessible; otherwise assigning `location.hash` is acceptable, but must create a normal history entry and let the home teardown restore `.skinHeader` before the destination renders.

NICE-TO-HAVE

17. **“Everything” library queries need an explicit performance policy.** Quote: “rails hold everything.” With no `Limit`, Shows and Movies can become expensive despite the current small library. State that this is intentional for v1, disable total-count work where supported (`EnableTotalRecordCount:false`), request only necessary fields/images, and document a future cap or pagination threshold.

18. **Required fields should be enumerated by section.** Quote: “Fields=`ChildCount`” and “same with `IncludeItemTypes=Movie`.” Specify all non-default fields relied upon: Continue Watching needs `Overview` and usable image/user-data/runtime metadata; Shows needs `ChildCount`; Movies needs runtime metadata. This prevents a later server/client change from silently producing `0 seasons`, missing runtimes, or incorrect remaining-time labels.

19. **Remaining-time formatting needs clamping rules.** Quote: “`N min left`.” Use `max(0, RunTimeTicks - PlaybackPositionTicks)` and define behavior when runtime is absent or playback position exceeds runtime. Avoid displaying negative time or `0 min left` for effectively completed items; fall back to season/episode metadata or runtime-only text.

20. **Image fallback behavior is incomplete.** Quote: “episode Primary → Backdrop fallback” and “poster cards (Primary image).” Specify placeholder rendering and `img.onerror` behavior for every card type. For episode landscape art, also consider inherited series backdrop/thumb metadata because episode `Primary` may be missing. Keep empty poster cards navigable and labelled rather than removing the entire title.

21. **Accessibility semantics need more precision.** Quote: “If that split is awkward to implement accessibly…” Choose the accessible model in the spec instead of leaving it optional: make the card’s text/art a single Details link or button and the play chip a separate ≥44px button with an item-specific label such as “Resume Arcane, episode 3.” Avoid nested interactive elements. Give rails labelled regions and visible focus styles, not only touch behavior.

22. **Loading behavior should be specified.** Quote: “skip a section silently if its fetch fails or is empty.” Silent degradation is reasonable after completion, but an initially blank page can look broken during first boot. Define either lightweight skeletons or a single non-blocking loading state, then remove failed/empty sections without an error toast. If all requests fail, retain the top bar and show a modest retry affordance rather than an empty black page.

23. **Verification should include the actual default-boot and restored-tab cases.** Quote: “Home renders our view.” Add tests for: cold authenticated launch beginning with an empty hash; `ApiClient` present before user ID; restored Favorites tab; sign-out/sign-in without a hash change; rapid Home → Details → Back repeated three times; and Home → Search/Profile → Back. Verify exactly one overlay, one body class, no live observers/timers from prior generations, restored header state, and restored scroll positions.
